news.title: OpenWorld Announces Pricing of $3.5 Million Registered Direct Offering Priced At-The-Market Under Nasdaq Rules
news.description: LAKE MARY, Fla., Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- OpenWorld, Inc. (NASDAQ: OPNW) ('OpenWorld' or the 'Company'), an innovation company advancing global real-world asset ('RWA”) tokenization, today announced that it has entered into a securities purchase agreement with a single institutional investor for the purchase and sale of 2,517,985 shares of common stock (or pre-funded warrants in-lieu thereof), together with Series A warrants to purchase up to an aggregate of 2,517,985 shares of common stock, and Series B warrants to purchase up to an aggregate of 2,517,985 shares of common stock, in a registered direct offering priced at-the-market under Nasdaq rules. Each share of common stock and accompanying warrants are being sold together at a combined purchase price of $1.39. The Series A warrants will have an exercise price of $1.53 per share, will be subject to shareholder approval, and will expire five years from the date of shareholder approval. The Series B warrants will have an exercise price of $1.39 per share, will be subject to shareholder approval, and will expire eighteen months from the date of shareholder approval. The Series B warrants will be callable by the Company, subject to certain conditions, if the daily trading price of the common stock exceeds 400% of the exercise price and the average daily trading volume of the common stock exceeds $1.0 million over a period of ten consecutive trading days. Upon a call, any portion of the Series B warrants not exercised within ten trading days following the holder's receipt of the call notice will be cancelled.

news.title: US SEC proposes wider retail investor access to private assets amid risk concerns
news.description: The SEC has proposed new rules to expand access to private assets typically available only to wealthy investors. These rules aim to allow more professionals to qualify as accredited investors, which may lead to higher returns. Critics express concern that this move could expose retail investors to significant risks and fees. Additionally, proposed changes would allow closed-end funds to redeem shares more frequently and offer varied share classes.
